 News › News News › Bihar Government School News: Female teachers can get special leave approved by headmasters at schoo… Bihar Government School News: Female teachers can get special leave approved by headmasters at school level; Vaishali DEO issues clarification during exam period
 Adhya Sarna Updated: Nov 20, 2026, 08:45 IST The District Education Officer (DEO) of Vaishali in Bihar has issued an order that allows school principals to approve special leave (SL) for female teachers The District Education Officer (DEO) of Vaishali in Bihar has issued an order that allows school principals to approve special leave (SL) for female teachers at their own level. The order, dated November 18, 2026, partially amends an earlier memo from the same office.
 It was shared on X by the Bihar Shikshak Sangh, a teachers' organisation, in a post describing it as a major change to leave rules for government school staff.
 What did the Vaishali DEO order say? 
 According to the order shown in the post, the office of the District Education Officer, Vaishali, has amended paragraph 2 of its earlier memo No. 677/Exam, dated November 18, 2026. Under the new instruction, principals of the concerned schools are directed to approve special leave for female teachers at their own level, in line with departmental instructions. 
 The order adds that all other directions in the earlier memo remain unchanged.
 The order is signed by the DEO and was sent to all principals and in-charge principals of government and government-aided schools in the district. It was also copied to block education officers, who have been asked to ensure continuous monitoring of schools in their areas, and to the District Programme Officer. I could not view the earlier memo, so what paragraph 2 originally required is not clear from the post.
 Does the order apply across all Bihar? 
 No, the order was issued by the Vaishali district office, so it applies to schools under that district's jurisdiction. Teachers in other districts should follow instructions from their own DEOs and the state Education Department. The post's description of a ‘major change to Bihar government school holidays’ is also loose: the order concerns the authority to approve leave for female teachers, not the school holiday calendar.
 What is special leave for women in Bihar? 
 Bihar introduced special leave for regular women employees in 1992, during the tenure of former chief minister Lalu Prasad Yadav, providing two days of leave every month. In May 2026, the state extended two days of monthly special leave to women working on contractual and outsourcing arrangements, and said Bihar was the first state in the country to do so. Reports describe the facility as a form of menstrual leave.
 The Vaishali order does not specify the number of days or the conditions of the leave. 
 It refers only to "departmental instructions", so the entitlement itself remains as laid down by the state government.
 Why does the approval authority matter for teachers? 
 Leave approval rules in Bihar's schools have been changing. Under the online system through the e-Shikshakosh portal announced in 2025, headmasters approve applications from assistant and special teachers, while block education officers handle requests from headmasters. Letting principals sanction special leave at the school level can shorten the approval process, since teachers do not have to wait for decisions from higher offices.
 It also puts more responsibility on principals, who must apply departmental rules correctly and keep records.
 The order also arrives at a time when the state is revising its leave rules for women teachers. The education minister has told the Assembly that the new framework would bring clearer guidelines and transparency in the approval and management of leave, so that female employees receive their salaries and entitlements on time.
 What should female teachers do next? 
 Teachers in Vaishali should check the new order with their school principal and confirm how to submit applications, whether on paper or through the online portal. They should also keep copies of approvals for their service records. Principals, for their part, should ensure that applications are dealt with promptly and in line with the rules. If any doubt arises over eligibility or the number of days, the school can seek clarification from the block education office.
